<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915834_theRebbe_708" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915834_theRebbe_708__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the header and date of the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Motzaei Shabbat Parshat Vayeishev,</t>
    <t s="2">Erev Rosh Chodesh Tevet — in his room — 5738*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the distinction between "great peace" and ordinary peace, and that "lovers of Your Torah" refers to love stemming from the Giver of the Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"Great peace have those who love Your Torah..."1,</t>
    <t s="1">And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, precisely analyzes in his maamar beginning with the words "Zot"</t>
    <t s="2">[of Shabbat Parshat Vayeishev 57042,</t>
    <t s="3">which is a continuation of the maamar beginning "Padeh b'Shalom" of Yud-Tes Kislev 57043],</t>
    <t s="4">what is the concept of "great peace,"</t>
    <t s="5">from which it is understood that there is an ordinary peace</t>
    <t s="6">[and in the language of the maamar there — "a small peace"4]</t>
    <t s="7">and a great peace.</t>
    <t s="8">And also, what is [the meaning of] "those who love Your Torah"?</t>
    <t s="9">Is not Torah wisdom and understanding</t>
    <t s="10">[as it is written5,</t>
    <t s="11">"For it is your wisdom and your understanding"]</t>
    <t s="12">and it would be fitting to use the language of study, which is attributed to wisdom and understanding, and not the language of love.</t>
    <t s="13">And he explains there6,</t>
    <t s="14">that "those who love Your Torah" means that they love the Torah not only from the perspective of the Torah itself</t>
    <t s="15">(from the perspective of the wisdom within it)</t>
    <t s="16">but rather from the perspective of the Giver of the Torah</t>
    <t s="17">("those who love Your Torah"7).</t>
    <t s="18">And this is [the meaning of] "Great peace have those who love Your Torah,"</t>
    <t s="19">that the peace which is made through the study of Torah</t>
    <t s="20">(ordinary [study])</t>
    <t s="21">is an ordinary peace</t>
    <t s="22">(a small peace),</t>
    <t s="23">but not so for "those who love Your Torah,"</t>
    <t s="24">when the study of Torah is not only with love of Torah but also with love of G-d</t>
    <t s="25">[and it is understood that this also [includes] love of Israel,</t>
    <t s="26">for love of Israel is a vessel for love of G-d8,</t>
    <t s="27">to the extent that they are entirely one9],</t>
    <t s="28">then a great peace is drawn down</t>
    <t s="29">(which is above ordinary peace).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the concept of "lovers of Your Torah" is achieved through the prior service of prayer, which brings one to love of G-d.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the concept of "those who love Your Torah"</t>
    <t s="2">(that the love for Torah is from the perspective of the Giver of the Torah)</t>
    <t s="3">is explained in the aforementioned maamar6,</t>
    <t s="4">that this is accomplished through the prior service of prayer.</t>
    <t s="5">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="6">for the primary service is love of G-d, as the statement10</t>
    <t s="7">"There is no worship like the worship of love."</t>
    <t s="8">And this also applies to the line of service,</t>
    <t s="9">the entirety of the concept of service, the concept of prayer,</t>
    <t s="10">for the service and toil of prayer is11</t>
    <t s="11">to come to love of G-d.</t>
    <t s="12">And this is that the concept of "those who love Your Torah" is through the prior service of prayer,</t>
    <t s="13">for through prayer one comes to love of G-d,</t>
    <t s="14">and through this he becomes "one who loves Your Torah,"</t>
    <t s="15">[meaning] that his love for Torah is from the perspective of the Giver of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="16">as above.</t>
    <t s="17">And this is also what is explained in many places12</t>
    <t s="18">(regarding the prayer of Abba Binyamin, "May my prayer be near my bed"13)</t>
    <t s="19">that the virtue of Torah study is specifically when it comes after prayer</t>
    <t s="20">[although the service of prayer is a distinct line and Torah study is a distinct line],</t>
    <t s="21">for through the prior service of prayer, the study is in a more elevated manner,</t>
    <t s="22">even to the level of "those who love Your Torah."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
